title: A Diverging History Clock Is Not a Blow-up Proof: Lean-Checked Lemmas Showing Why a Section 10 Navier-Stokes Argument Does Not Establish Fefferman (C) or (D)
description: Negative-result note; no claim toward the Clay Millennium problem. Explains why a 'quadratic history clock' diverging as T to infinity does not establish finite-time blow-up (Fefferman C/D), and checks the scalar real-analysis facts in Lean 4 + Mathlib: bound gives int f <= MT; int f <= (T + int f^2)/2; constant-M history diverges at infinity while BKM integral MT is finite; (T*-t)^-1 and its square not integrable on [0,T*]. 8 theorems, no sorry, standard axioms only. No Navier-Stokes equations or BKM theorem formalized.
